title: RESET safety: define state machine, enforce nonce lifecycle, fix GEN_IV FIPS boundary
description:
Three related nonce/IV safety problems grouped together because they all require the same human decision about RESET semantics:

1. RESET STATE MACHINE UNDEFINED: CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_RESET 're-arms a finalized session' but the spec does not say what state survives. If the IV/nonce is preserved across RESET for AES-CBC or AES-GCM, the next operation reuses the same IV under the same key. For GCM this is catastrophic: two ciphertexts under the same key+nonce allows full plaintext recovery and key extraction.

2. GEN_IV FIPS BOUNDARY: CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_GEN_IV calls get_random_bytes() (kernel CSPRNG) regardless of which provider is active. For the wolfssl FIPS provider path, this generates the IV outside the wolfCrypt FIPS boundary. FIPS 140-3 may require all entropy feeding into a FIPS operation to come from an approved DRBG (wc_RNG_GenerateBlock).

3. GCM NONCE LENGTH NOT VALIDATED: SET_IV accepts up to CRYPTO2DEV_IV_MAXLEN (32) bytes. The NIST GCM spec requires a 96-bit (12-byte) nonce for the standard construction; longer nonces require GHASH derivation and change the security properties. The framework does not reject a 16-byte nonce for GCM.

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED:

(a) What state does RESET preserve?
  Option A: Preserve algo + key; require new SET_IV (and SET_AAD if AEAD) before next write(). write() before SET_IV after RESET returns -EINVAL.
  Option B: Preserve algo only; require full INIT-equivalent re-keying. (Effectively: RESET = close + open + INIT with same algo, cheaper allocation.)
  Option C: RESET resets everything — equivalent to close + reopen. Simplest spec, slightly more expensive.
  Recommendation: Option A is the most useful (avoids re-keying) while being safe if SET_IV is enforced.

(b) GEN_IV: should the wolfssl provider path use wc_RNG_GenerateBlock instead of get_random_bytes?
  Option A: Yes — GEN_IV becomes a provider callback ops->gen_iv(), wolfssl calls wc_RNG_GenerateBlock, kcapi calls get_random_bytes.
  Option B: get_random_bytes is acceptable; the kernel CSPRNG is SP 800-90A-equivalent and wolfCrypt is consuming the output, not generating it independently.
  This is a FIPS consultant question (see human_task/006) but the code decision follows from it.

(c) GCM nonce length: should SET_IV validate ivlen against the algorithm?
  Option A: Yes — framework rejects ivlen != 12 for gcm(aes). Strict and correct.
  Option B: Pass through to provider; provider rejects at wc_AesGcmSetKey/SetIV time. Less coupling between framework and algo knowledge.

Work items once decisions are made:
- Document RESET state machine in DESIGN.md
- Enforce IV-required check in write() after RESET (if option A)
- Make GEN_IV a provider callback (if option A for FIPS boundary)
- Add per-algo ivlen validation in SET_IV handler (if option A for GCM nonce)
close_reason: All three sub-decisions implemented: (a) RESET state machine with iv_set enforcement; (b) gen_iv provider callback for FIPS-boundary IV generation; (c) GCM nonce passthrough to provider (no change needed)
